privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.metaDescription: How Champagne de l'Aube collects and protects your personal data: forms, newsletter, processors (Brevo, Netlify), cookies and your rights.
privacy.intro: This page explains simply what personal data we collect on this website, why, who it is shared with and how to exercise your rights.

responsable.title: Data controller
responsable.text:
Champagne de l'Aube, Julien Mineo, sole trader (micro-entreprise), SIRET 527 744 528 00029. Administrative office: {adresse}.
Contact: contact@champagnedelaube.fr

donnees.title: Data collected
donnees.text:
• Forms (quote, booking, registration, contact): name, email and/or phone, business or company, town, number of people, preferred date, message.
• Newsletter: email address, language, sign-up page and date of your consent.
• In all cases: confirmation that you are 18 or older, the website language and the page you are writing from.

finalites.title: Why this data is used
finalites.text:
• To reply to your request and prepare a quote or booking (pre-contractual measures).
• To follow up our exchange: your contact details are saved in our address book (Brevo), sorted by profile (professional, company, private client, winemaker) (legitimate interest). This does not subscribe you to the newsletter.
• To send you news, only if you asked for it and confirmed by clicking the link received by email (consent).
• To protect the forms against automated submissions (legitimate interest).

destinataires.title: Who has access to your data
destinataires.text:
Your data is never sold or rented. Only Julien Mineo has access to it, along with these technical providers (processors), for the needs of the website:
• Brevo (Sendinblue SAS, France): sending emails and address book. Data hosted in the European Union.
• Netlify (United States): website hosting. Transfers covered by the European Commission's standard contractual clauses.
• Sanity (United States): management of the website's texts and photos. No form data is stored there.
• Cloudflare Turnstile (if enabled): anti-bot protection for the forms, without advertising cookies.

conservation.title: How long
conservation.text:
• Requests and contacts: 3 years after our last exchange, then deleted.
• Newsletter: until you unsubscribe (a link is included in every email). Proof of your consent is kept as long as you are subscribed.

droits.title: Your rights
droits.text:
At any time you can access your data, have it corrected or deleted, object to its use, restrict its use, obtain a copy, or withdraw your consent to the newsletter. Simply write to contact@champagnedelaube.fr.
If you believe your rights are not respected, you can lodge a complaint with the French data protection authority, the CNIL (www.cnil.fr).

cepagesPage.intro: Champagne is made from eight grapes permitted by the appellation: three major ones, pinot noir, chardonnay and meunier, and five rarer ones. To taste them, join one of [our tastings](/tasting-troyes) or discover [our selection](/vignerons).

troyesPage.metaDescription: Troyes, capital of the Aube and city of the Counts of Champagne: its history, the Montgueux vineyard 13 km away, the Côte des Bar and our private tastings.
troyesPage.intro: Capital of the Aube and former capital of the Counts of Champagne, Troyes has the vineyards right on its doorstep: the hill of Montgueux is about ten kilometres away. This is where we hold our private tastings of growers' champagnes from the Aube, hoping you will come to love our city as much as our wines.
troyesPage.histoire1: In the Middle Ages, Troyes was the capital of the Counts of Champagne. The city prospered thanks to the Champagne fairs: six great fairs punctuated the year in the region, two in Provins, one in Lagny, one in Bar-sur-Aube and two in Troyes, the “hot fair” in summer and the “cold fair” in autumn. Merchants and money-changers came from all over Europe.
troyesPage.histoire2: Seen from the air, the old town is shaped like a champagne cork, and locals call it “le Bouchon” (the cork). Its streets are lined with half-timbered houses, many rebuilt after the great fire of 1524. A walk to take with your head up, before or after a tasting.

troyesPage.vignobleTexte: In Montgueux, the chalk hill is planted mostly with chardonnay. Further south, the Côte des Bar is the kingdom of pinot noir, and Les Riceys produces three appellations: champagne, coteaux champenois and rosé des Riceys.
troyesPage.venirTitre: Passing through Troyes? Champagne comes to you
troyesPage.venirTexte1: No time to drive out to the vineyards? We bring the growers' champagnes of the Aube to you in Troyes, at your home or at a venue of your choice, with the stories of their villages and of the people who make them.
troyesPage.venirTexte2: With friends, family, for a special occasion or during a stay: tell us what you would enjoy, and we will put the tasting together with you.
troyesPage.gastro1: Troyes has its specialities. The best known is andouillette de Troyes, made with pork. Chaource, a PDO soft cheese with a bloomy rind, is made south of Troyes, in the Aube and the neighbouring Yonne.
troyesPage.gastro2: With chaource, a grower's champagne makes a lovely pairing, and rosé des Riceys goes well with local cooking. For more ideas, see our [champagne food pairing recipes](/recettes-accords-mets-champagne).

faq.q1: Where can I find vineyards near Troyes?
faq.r1: The hill of Montgueux, about ten kilometres west of Troyes, is the nearest vineyard. Bar-sur-Seine, in the heart of the Côte des Bar, is some thirty kilometres to the south-east.
faq.q2: Can I do a champagne tasting in Troyes?
faq.r2: Yes: we organise private tastings of growers' champagnes from the Aube, in Troyes, at your home or at a venue of your choice. Tell us about your plans and we will come back to you with a proposal.
faq.q3: Why is the centre of Troyes called “le Bouchon”?
faq.r3: Because, seen from the air, the layout of the old town is shaped like a champagne cork.
